issues.description: The Developer initializer signature in the solution repository does not match the problem statement or the template. The problem statement and template define/initiate Developer with two parameters (name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?). In the solution, the initializer has an extra parameter age: Int (init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?, age: Int)), while the solution's Client still constructs Developer using the two-parameter form. This creates a structural mismatch between problem/template and solution and an internal inconsistency in the solution repository (Client vs Developer). Students comparing template and solution would be confused and the solution as provided will not compile as-is.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution's Developer initializer match the problem statement and template by removing the extraneous age parameter. Change the initializer in solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift to: init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) { ... } and keep the existing print(self.swiftExperienceDescription()). Ensure Client usages remain as two-argument calls. Alternatively (if age was intentionally required), update the problem statement, template, and all client code to include the age parameter consistently — but the simpler fix is to remove the unintended age parameter from the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Developer initializer that accepts two parameters (name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?). The solution's Developer initializer instead has a third parameter age: Int (init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?, age: Int)). This introduces an unexpected parameter name/parameter-list difference for the same conceptual entity (the Developer initializer). Students mapping the requirement (create Developer with name and optional monthsOfSwiftExperience and print the experience description from the initializer) to the provided solution will be confused: the extra 'age' parameter is not mentioned in the exercise, and it breaks consistency with the template and the problem description (and even causes a mismatch with the solution's own Client usage).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution's Developer initializer with the problem statement and template by removing the extraneous 'age' parameter. Change the initializer signature in the solution to init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) and keep the required print(self.swiftExperienceDescription()) call inside it. This preserves the intended exercise API and removes the unexpected naming/parameter mismatch.
